subtopics.title: The Four Factors and the Four Rewards

questions.question: Which factor-and-reward matching is completely correct?
options: Natural resources — rent; labour — wages and salaries; capital — interest; entrepreneurship — profit
Natural resources — wages; labour — profit; capital — rent; entrepreneurship — interest
Natural resources — interest; labour — rent; capital — profit; entrepreneurship — wages
Each factor earns dividends in proportion to its size

questions.question: "Capital means the oven, not the overdraft" expresses the point that:
options: Ovens are more valuable than money
Economic capital is REAL capital — produced means of production such as machines and buildings — while money is merely a claim that can buy them
Only heavy machinery counts as capital

questions.question: In the factor market of the circular flow:
options: Firms sell finished goods to households
Households supply the four factors they own, and firms pay rent, wages, interest and profit in return

questions.question: Dividends are not a factor remuneration because:
options: They are too irregular to record
They are a form of interest
They are profit that has already been earned as the reward to entrepreneurship, now being passed on to shareholders

subtopics.title: Natural Resources and Labour Under the Microscope

questions.question: A corner trading site beside a busy Soweto intersection commands fierce rent because:
options: Its total supply is FIXED — many traders want that exact spot and nobody can produce a second one, so demand alone sets the rent
The site was expensive to construct

questions.question: Labour's PERISHABILITY means that:
options: Today's unworked hours are lost forever and cannot be stored — which is why unemployment is a permanent loss, not a delay

questions.question: Under the Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Act, the minerals beneath a farm belong to:
options: The farmer who owns the surface
The mining house that discovers them
The STATE, with companies mining under licensed rights
The traditional authority of the district

questions.question: Mass unemployment existing beside unfilled high-skill vacancies is evidence of:
options: A skills MISMATCH — the skills workers offer are not the skills employers demand

questions.question: The Pietermaritzburg furniture factory sells R6 000 000 of output and buys in R2 400 000 of timber, fabric, electricity and transport. Its VALUE ADDED is:
Out of value added of R3 600 000 the firm pays wages of R2 250 000, rent of R330 000, interest of R270 000 and sets aside R270 000 for depreciation. Profit is:
Profit is called a RESIDUAL because:
options: It is the smallest of the payments
It is whatever remains after the contractual payments to the other factors — and the remainder can be negative
It is set by the shareholders in advance

questions.question: The R2 400 000 of bought-in timber and electricity is excluded from the factor share-out because:
options: It is an overhead, not a cost
It is INTERMEDIATE consumption that already generated wages and profits inside the sawmill and the utility — counting it again would double count

subtopics.title: Local Economic Planning, Access and Empowerment Procurement

questions.question: The Integrated Development Plan (IDP) is:
options: The plan every municipality must adopt and revisit annually, with local economic development written inside it

questions.question: Insecure land tenure blocks access to the other factors because:
options: Untitled land may not be farmed
Without registered title there is nothing to pledge as COLLATERAL, so lenders refuse and the venture dies unborn
Municipalities tax untitled land more heavily

questions.question: The B-BBEE scorecard measures a firm on:
options: Ownership, management control, skills development, enterprise and supplier development, and socio-economic development

questions.question: The 80/20 and 90/10 systems of the Preferential Procurement Policy Framework Act mean that:
options: Tenders are split between two winning bidders
The state pays a 20 per cent deposit up front
Only 10 per cent of bids are read
Most tender points go to price and a fixed remainder to defined goals such as transformation, with 90/10 used for larger contracts

subtopics.title: The Salon, the Stylist, the Clippers and the Owner

questions.question: In the container salon, the clippers, dryers, chairs and card machine are:
options: CAPITAL — made things that exist to produce haircuts, financed by a loan that charges interest

questions.question: The person who spotted the busy strip, borrowed for the container, hires the stylists and absorbs the loss when the geyser bursts supplies:
"Money is not capital" means, in the salon's case:
options: The R150 000 loan in the account is not the factor of production — the clippers and chairs it bought are
Only fixed property counts as capital

questions.question: The salon takes R45 000 in a month and spends R13 500 on shampoo, colour, electricity and airtime from other businesses. The value it ADDED is:
Wages of R15 000, rent of R4 500, interest of R2 500 and R3 500 set aside for wear come out of R31 500. The owner keeps:
The payment queue in the salon shows that:
options: The owner draws a guaranteed salary first
Everyone else is paid FIRST at pre-agreed amounts and the owner LAST at an amount nobody promised — which is why the owner makes the decisions
Interest is only paid in profitable months
Wages depend on the month's takings

questions.question: The R13 500 of shampoo and electricity is left out of the salon's value added because:
options: It already paid a wage at the warehouse and a profit at the utility — counting it again would count the same rand twice

subtopics.title: Whose Town Is It — Planning, Doors and Tenders

questions.question: "A valley with perfect citrus and no juicing plant railcars its oranges away and buys the juice back" illustrates:
options: The purpose of local economic planning — combining a district's own factors locally so the value added stays in the valley
The law of comparative advantage only
The repo rate's effect on farming

questions.question: The three would-be caterers with the same plan show that access to the factors depends on:
options: The originality of the business plan
Collateral, information and transport — not the quality of the idea

questions.question: Attending the ward meeting has economic weight because:
options: The meeting sets the repo rate
The plan is written with or without you, and the paving, clinic and market stalls go where the plan points

questions.question: The economic logic of empowerment procurement is that:
options: The state should always accept the cheapest bid
Charity is the state's main duty
Tenders create competition among big firms only
Demand creates factor incomes — so aiming a share of the state's enormous purchasing at excluded suppliers redirects income toward them
